plain.text: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices to anoint Jesus' body. Very early on Sunday, at sunrise, they went to the tomb, wondering who would roll away the heavy stone. But it had already been rolled away. Inside, they saw a young man in a white robe and were alarmed. He said, "Don't be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here. Go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you." Trembling and bewildered, the women fled from the tomb and said nothing to anyone, because they were afraid.

Many of the oldest manuscripts of Mark end at verse 8. Other manuscripts include these closing verses. They say that Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons. She told those who had been with him, but they did not believe her.
Afterwards, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked in the country. They went back and told the rest, who did not believe them either.

Later Jesus appeared to the eleven as they were eating. He rebuked them for their unbelief. He told them, "Go into all the world and preach the good news to all creation. Whoever believes and is baptised will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned." He said signs would accompany those who believe, including driving out demons, speaking in new tongues and healing the sick.

After speaking to them, the Lord Jesus was taken up into heaven and sat at the right hand of God. The disciples went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked with them, confirming his word by the signs that went with it.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus has risen from the dead, just as he said, and his followers are sent to tell the world.
points: Women find the tomb empty, and a messenger says, "He has risen! He is not here."
The oldest manuscripts end with the women's fear and amazement; later endings tell of appearances.
Jesus sends his followers into all the world with the good news.
summary.reflection: The women were told to go and tell, even "Peter", who had denied Jesus. What does it mean that the message included him?
